conclusions: Cached group unions reduce the sampled moving-light manager component from 774 to 464 microseconds (about 40%). Total desktop submission still favours original instances; keep batches off by default.
119 checks pass in each of Compatibility budget 8, budget 4 and Forward+ bypass; every paired live fixture frame is byte-exact.

The nine-pixel shadow/contact residual is reproduced without MultiMesh, solely by reinserting original render instances. The resulting image is byte-identical to the previous batched capture. All nine traced pixels meet overlapping stwa13/hadoganwall01 geometry.

This attributes the reproduced nine pixels only. Modern-camera timing captures still differ from originals by 16 pixels without added lights and 2 with four; 14 pixels persist after restoration. Their separate cause has not been established. The cache preserves those results exactly.
Near-plane changes are diagnostic only and do not justify changing production clipping.
Forward+ fixture with a temporary ReflectionProbe still reports 7 leaked Texture RIDs at shutdown. The production manager bypasses Forward+; this is not a leak-free acceptance claim.
Read-only apply check passed against the other active checkout, including uncommitted story/co-op work. No patch was applied and checked target state was unchanged.
This work makes no sun-policy change: desktop remains continuous; held Android/web remains a replaceable fallback per user direction.
